name: Pattern Energy Group LP
headquarters: San Francisco, California, United States (1088 Sansome Street — the legal, accounts-payable and FERC compliance address, and 'Global HQ' on the company's own pages) with the development headquarters, Operations Control Center and the chief executive in Houston, Texas (888 Westheimer Road); 2026 press releases are datelined Houston, San Francisco and Toronto
employees: 'More than 800' (September 2025) — 670 Pattern Energy employees plus 186 at the Solect Energy and Dynamic Energy distributed-generation affiliates at 31 December 2024; 150 in Houston (June 2023)

ownership.ticker: Private (CPP Investments majority shareholder since the March 2020 take-private; APG Asset Management for ABP and Australian Retirement Trust consortium since June 2025; Pattern management). Formerly NASDAQ: PEGI / TSX: PEG, 2013–2020

summary: **BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Pattern Energy is the largest privately owned renewables and transmission developer in North America by its own account and, since 18 June 2026, the owner-operator of SunZia — 3,650 MW of New Mexico wind and the 550-mile, ±525 kV, 3,000 MW voltage-source HVDC line that carries it to Arizona and California, financed on USD 11 billion of non-recourse debt and about USD 2.7 billion of structured and preferred equity from HASI and Nuveen; its ownership moved twice in twelve months — an APG/ABP and Australian Retirement Trust consortium bought Riverstone's founding stake (closed 9 June 2025) and the share-based purchase of CPP Investments' Cordelio Power (closed 2 April 2026) took CPP-led institutional ownership to 69.1% by CPP's own statement — and no sale, secondary or IPO process is on the record, while the company publishes no revenue, earnings or leverage figure. **BACKGROUND.** Founded 2009 in San Francisco by Riverstone Holdings and a management team from Babcock & Brown's North American renewables business (Mike Garland, Hunter Armistead); listed the operating company as Pattern Energy Group Inc. in 2013 (USD 352 million IPO); taken private by CPP Investments on 16 March 2020 at USD 26.75 a share (enterprise value about USD 6.1 billion) and recombined with the development company. Fleet per the 2025 sustainability report: 32 utility-scale facilities, 6,047 MW installed (4,148 MW owned excluding tax equity) at end-2024 across the United States, Canada and Mexico; per the company after Cordelio, 'more than 40 facilities' and 'nearly 12,000 MW of operating and in-construction capacity' (46 facilities and about 12 GW installed on the About page), with a development portfolio the company variously states at 25 GW (December 2024), 30 GW (September 2025) and 40 GW (2026). Transmission: Western Spirit (155 miles, 345 kV) built and sold to PNM in 2021; SunZia operating; Southern Spirit (320 miles, ±525 kV HVDC, ERCOT to the Southeast, USD 2.6 billion) with Louisiana's certificate but no Mississippi decision and construction pushed to 2029; Bolo (24 miles, 800 MW) and Silver Rock (330 miles, Utah–Nevada, BLM scoping opened 2 September 2026) in development. Chief executive Hunter Armistead since 1 January 2023; CFO Matthew Rhodes since October 2024; a new chief operating officer, chief legal officer and chief people officer appeared on the leadership page in 2026 without releases. Collection gap: no ownership percentages beyond CPP's 69.1% sentence, no financial statements, no independent SunZia cost figure, and an S&P item dated 8 August 2026 on USD 700 million of Pattern Energy Operations senior notes that could not be read.
ecosystemRole: The corpus's second transmission developer and its first at scale: Pattern is both a multi-gigawatt wind and solar owner in the storage-developers-and-IPP class and the sponsor of the one long-haul VSC HVDC corridor in the United States to reach commercial operation. On the grid-equipment side it is Hitachi Energy's reference customer for HVDC Light and the buyer of 674 GE Vernova turbines; on the utilities side it is the merchant transmission owner that California's grid operator absorbed through the Subscriber PTO model, a wholesale seller to SRP, Shell, the University of California, LADWP and eight community choice aggregators, and the developer Entergy Mississippi fought at the state commission. Its data-centre exposure is indirect — Microsoft (Winfield, Crossover), Amazon (Fowler Ridge) and Digital Realty (Phoenix) as offtakers and a Silver Rock line pitched at Utah and Nevada data-centre load — with no announced hyperscaler campus deal of its own. Against Grid United it is the comparable that has permits, customers, financing and an operating asset; against Invenergy it is the pension-owned, not founder-owned, version of the same integrated developer-transmission model.

productsAndServices.name: SunZia Wind and Transmission — 3,650 MW of New Mexico wind on a 550-mile, 3,000 MW ±525 kV HVDC line to Arizona (operating since June 2026)
productsAndServices.category: Integrated wind and merchant HVDC transmission (flagship)
productsAndServices.description: The company's description: 'SunZia, the largest renewable energy infrastructure project in U.S. history is fully operational' (18 June 2026) — 'an approximately 3,650-megawatt (MW) wind project' in Torrance, Lincoln and San Miguel counties and a '550-mile ±525 kV high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission line between central New Mexico and south-central Arizona with the capacity to transport 3,000 MW', 'the first overhead HVDC transmission line built in the United States in the last 30 years'. Pattern acquired the transmission project from SouthWestern Power Group on 18 July 2022, having already been awarded its full 3,000 MW of capacity for its wind; the BLM record of decision followed on 18 May 2023 'after over 16 years of development', notice to proceed and groundbreaking on 1 September 2023, and the USD 11 billion non-recourse financing closed 27 December 2023 — 'an integrated construction loan and letter of credit facility, two separate term facilities, an operating phase letter of credit facility, an innovative tax equity term loan facility and a holding company loan facility'. Suppliers and contractors: Hitachi Energy (HVDC Light voltage-source converters and MACH control), Quanta Services (turnkey line), Blattner (wind, 'more than 900 turbines, ten substations'), GE Vernova (674 turbines) and Vestas (242). Independent record of the in-service date: WECC's 2026 progress report says the line 'was energized in 2025 and has been undergoing testing through Q1 2026' with in-service planned March 2026; EIA dates commercial operation to June 2026 with 916 turbines and 2,131 MW designated for Southern California via Palo Verde; CAISO's allocation is 2,100 MW of the 3,650 MW and the line joined CAISO under the Subscriber Participating Transmission Owner model (3,021 MW, FERC Docket ER23-2917). Offtakers named by the company: Shell Energy North America and the University of California (May 2023), Clean Power Alliance (575 MW, 15 years, November 2023), Salt River Project (600 MW — 400 MW from autumn 2026 rising to 600 MW by summer 2027, July 2026), Ava Community Energy (over 250 MW), Central Coast Community Energy, CleanPowerSF, Riverside Public Utilities and Silicon Valley Clean Energy; per-offtaker volumes beyond CPA and SRP are not public. Capital beside the debt: HASI's USD 1.2 billion structured equity (closed October 2025, 'expected to ultimately finance over 2.6 GW') and Nuveen Energy Infrastructure Credit's USD 546 million preferred equity (1 July 2026; 'approached $1.5 billion across four investments' with co-investors, including 'the preferred tax equity for SunZia North').
highlights: Capacity is stated two ways and both are real: 3,515 MW nameplate at order (674 GE 3.6-154 plus 242 Vestas V163-4.5) in 2023 financing documents and Quanta's 10-K, 3,650 MW in 2026 statements by Pattern, Hitachi, Nuveen and EIA (EIA's is net summer capacity from Form 860M)

On the CAISO side the line contributed to a wind record of 7,122 MW on 15 May 2026, 20% above the prior record, while still in test; CAISO's own blog calls it 'a plus for reliability and affordability' because the New Mexico wind 'strengthens during late afternoon and evening hours when solar declines'

The San Pedro Valley litigation is live but not injunctive: the Ninth Circuit reversed the dismissal of the Tohono O'odham Nation, San Carlos Apache Tribe, Archaeology Southwest and Center for Biological Diversity NHPA claim on 27 May 2025, holding the BLM's limited notices to proceed were final agency action; the plaintiffs' summary-judgment motion asking the court to 'nullify BLM decisions authorizing construction' has been pending before Judge Zipps since 13 March 2026, with the line operating throughout

Cost: the company says 'on time and on budget' against the USD 11 billion financing and cites a USD 20.5 billion lifetime economic benefit study; no independent final-cost figure exists. Collection gap: neither the exact energisation date of the line nor the wind phases' commercial-operation dates are published — only 'fully operational' on 18 June 2026

Follow-on lines in the same corridor: Bolo (24 miles, 345 kV, 800 MW, linking the Western Spirit switchyard on PNM's system to SunZia's Pete Heinrich switchyard; construction 2026 and operation 2027 per the open-solicitation site, but the January 2026 open solicitation 'has been postponed until further notice') and Pattern's stated intent to bid into the RioSol capacity solicitation (Southwestern Power Group's parallel 1,600 MW AC line, construction from late 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: The only privately financed long-haul VSC HVDC corridor operating in the United States; Invenergy's Grain Belt Express (5,000 MW, line-commutated, construction from 2026) and Grid United's North Plains Connector (3,000 MW, permitting) are the comparables, neither yet built. Champlain Hudson (Blackstone/TDI) and SunZia are the two lines Canary Media cites as the decade-plus precedents Grid United must repeat.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Wind sold under long-term PPAs to utilities, CCAs, an energy major and a university; transmission capacity held by the wind project (full 3,000 MW awarded to Pattern) and scheduled into CAISO under the Subscriber PTO model; project financed non-recourse with tax-equity, structured-equity and preferred-equity layers
targetSegments: California community choice aggregators and municipal utilities
Arizona utilities (Salt River Project via Pinal Central)
Corporate and institutional buyers (Shell Energy, University of California)
productsAndServices.roadmap: SRP deliveries 400 MW from autumn 2026 and 600 MW by summer 2027; Bolo construction 2026 and operation 2027 (solicitation postponed); RioSol capacity solicitation participation; ruling on the pending NHPA summary-judgment motion

productsAndServices.name: Operating wind, solar and storage fleet — about 12 GW installed across the United States, Canada and Mexico after Cordelio
productsAndServices.description: The company 'develops, constructs, owns, and operates high-quality wind, solar, transmission, and energy storage projects across North America'. The 2025 sustainability report's audited-style table gives 32 utility-scale facilities and 6,047 MW installed at 31 December 2024 (wind 5,664 MW; solar 383 MW; United States 3,768 MW, Canada 1,979 MW, Mexico 300 MW), of which 'Pattern Energy 3,695 MW (61%)' by ownership and, 'excluding tax equity, Pattern owns 4,148 MW'; generation 17,740 GWh in 2024 and 17,840 GWh in 2025. Named US wind (state, MW, COD): Western Spirit 1,051 MW, New Mexico, 2021 — four sites, 377 GE turbines, 'largest single-phase renewable energy project in U.S. history', offtakers including LADWP and Uniper; Broadview 324 MW, NM, 2017 (SCE, two 20-year PPAs); Gulf Wind 271 MW, Texas, repowered 2021 (Austin Energy, 20 years); Ocotillo 265 MW, California, 2012–13; Grady 221 MW, NM, 2019; Panhandle 1 and 2 400 MW, Texas, 2014; Post Rock 201 MW, Kansas (Evergy); Logan's Gap 200 MW, Texas; Lost Creek 168 MW, Missouri; Spring Valley 152 MW, Nevada (NV Energy); Amazon Wind Farm Fowler Ridge 150 MW, Indiana (AWS); Hatchet Ridge 101 MW, California (PG&E); Santa Isabel 101 MW, Puerto Rico; Stillwater 80 MW, Montana (NorthWestern, 25 years); plus SunZia. Canada (patterncanada.ca: '11 operating wind energy projects across 5 provinces', 'largest provider of wind to Ontario'): Henvey Inlet 300 MW (50/50 with Nigig Power, Henvey Inlet First Nation), Armow 180, South Kent 270, K2 270, Grand Renewable 149, Belle River 100, North Kent 99 (Ontario, with Samsung Renewable Energy and First Nation partners, IESO 20-year contracts); Meikle 179 MW, British Columbia (51% owned; BC Hydro 25 years); Mont Sainte-Marguerite 143 MW, Québec (Hydro-Québec 25 years); St. Joseph 138 MW, Manitoba (Manitoba Hydro 27 years); Lanfine 150 MW, Alberta, 2023 (West Fraser 10-year financial PPA for about half). Mexico: Tuli (2019) and Helios (2022) solar, 150 MW each, Zacatecas. Solar in the United States: Phoenix 83 MWac, Texas (2021; 65 MWac to Digital Realty, 12 years), Winfield 150 MWac, Missouri (September 2025; 100% to Microsoft, 15 years; Qcells modules), Silver State 50 MWac, Nevada, Box Canyon, Arizona. Storage: McHenry 20 MW, Illinois (2015) and, in development, the Amanecer Puerto Rico portfolio — a USD 489.4 million DOE Energy Dominance Financing loan closed in August 2026 for two standalone batteries totalling 220 MW at Arecibo and Santa Isabel with domestically sourced equipment. The Cordelio acquisition added 'approximately 1,550 megawatts of operating and in-construction assets, including 16 wind, solar, and energy storage projects'; the company does not list the sixteen, but fourteen are identifiable from portfolio pages added after closing — Glacier Sands 185 MW and Moraine Sands 171 MW (Illinois), Crossover 135 MW (Arkansas; 100% to Microsoft, 20 years, COD November 2025), Cedar Point (Colorado), McHenry, Box Canyon, Silver State, Winfield, and in Ontario Bluewater 60, Jericho 149, Summerhaven 124 and Conestogo 23 MW wind plus Sombra 20 and Moore 25 MW solar — with Axium Infrastructure holding 49% of the Ontario 'Denfield' portfolio since 2021.
highlights: Owned capacity is about two-thirds of installed capacity: tax-equity partners, First Nation and community co-owners (Henvey Inlet, Broughton, Ontario JVs), Samsung and Axium hold the rest — the number a buyer of Pattern's equity would value is 4,148 MW, not 6,047 MW (end-2024)

Offtake is long-dated and diversified — IESO and Hydro-Québec contracts of 20–30 years, SCE, PG&E, LADWP, NV Energy, Austin Energy, Evergy, NorthWestern, BC Hydro, Manitoba Hydro — with three named data-centre-adjacent buyers (Microsoft, AWS, Digital Realty) and no announced hyperscaler campus deal

Community and landowner payments are the one hard cash figure the company publishes: USD 156 million to local economies in 2025 (USD 93 million to landowners, USD 56 million property tax) and USD 140 million-plus in 2024

Japan (Green Power Investment, 337 MW operating and 192 MW under construction) was sold to NTT Anode Energy and JERA on 3 August 2023; the Mexico joint venture with CEMEX (2015) still shows two operating solar farms and no announced exit
The DOE Puerto Rico page states Pattern 'is working to deliver new gas-fired generation' for PREPA — a line the company's own channels do not carry
productsAndServices.positioning: Among the corpus's IPPs Pattern is the wind-heavy, Canada-heavy, pension-owned one: more Ontario wind than any other owner, a fleet whose median asset is a decade old, and a solar and storage book that is small next to Invenergy's or NextEra's. What sets it apart from every other IPP in the corpus is that it also owns the wires.

targetSegments: Regulated utilities and provincial buyers (IESO, Hydro-Québec, BC Hydro, Manitoba Hydro, NV Energy, SCE, PG&E)
Corporate buyers including data-centre operators (Microsoft, AWS, Digital Realty)
Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority (storage, and per DOE, gas)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Amanecer 220 MW Puerto Rico storage (DOE loan closed August 2026); Heritage Prairie Wind (Illinois, USD 2.1 billion, with Repsol; construction from June 2026, operation 2028) and Heritage Prairie Renewable (about 600 MW wind plus 300 MW solar with ConnectGen, 2027); Palomas Wind 800 MW, New Mexico (USD 2 billion; construction 2028, operation 2029); Lenawee 263 MW, Michigan (2028–29); Uplands two 300 MW wind, Wisconsin; The Shoals 500 MW wind plus 500 MW solar; Perryville 950 MW solar, Louisiana (2027–29); Big Island 440 MW solar, Arkansas (USD 750 million); Broughton 150 MW, Québec (30-year Hydro-Québec PPA, 2029); Osgood up to 200 MW, Québec (bid into Hydro-Québec's 2026 call, 2032); Argentia wind-to-hydrogen, Newfoundland (2030)

productsAndServices.name: Pattern Transmission — Southern Spirit, Silver Rock, Bolo and the completed lines
productsAndServices.description: 'Pattern Transmission is a highly experienced independent developer of high-voltage transmission infrastructure in North America... With the completion of SunZia, Pattern Transmission has now sponsored 30 percent of the high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission lines in the United States' and 'over 1,000 miles of high-voltage transmission developed and constructed'; the About page says '1100+ miles of transmission in operation and in development'. Completed: Western Spirit Transmission — a 155-mile 345 kV line developed with the New Mexico Renewable Energy Transmission Authority, energised 6 December 2021 and sold to PNM under a build-own-transfer agreement (PNM: closed 13 December 2021, USD 285 million net investment, 'up to 800 megawatts of new wind energy') with Pattern keeping the transmission rights; Henvey Inlet Transmission (104 km, 230 kV, Ontario, with Henvey Inlet First Nation); Western Interconnect (38 miles, New Mexico); and Trans Bay Cable (35-mile subsea HVDC, 400 MW, San Francisco) where 'the team at Pattern Transmission was an early sponsor and developer' but which Pattern does not own. In development: Southern Spirit — 'approximately 320-mile ±525 KV, ~3,000 MW high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission line connecting Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) and Southeastern transmission grids', from Garland Power & Light's Rusk–Panola line in Texas to a converter station in Choctaw County, Mississippi, 'more than $2.6 billion', 'Projected Schedule: 2029 Target Full Construction Start; 2032 Target In-Service Date' (the 2023 fact sheet said 'as early as late 2029'; the Louisiana order said 2026–2029). The Louisiana PSC granted its certificate in Order U-36669 on 14 August 2024 by 3:2 on reconsideration, on condition that 'no design or construction costs... be borne by the ratepayers of the state of Louisiana'; Louisiana's SB 108 (August 2024) restricts expropriation for lines outside an RTO plan; the Mississippi PSC's docket 2017-UA-79 was still 'CONTINUED' on the June 2026 agenda, so no Mississippi certificate exists; Entergy Mississippi's testimony argued the line would 'very likely harm' its customers; DOE selected the line for a Transmission Facilitation Program capacity contract of up to USD 360 million in October 2024, execution unconfirmed. Silver Rock — 'an approximately 330-mile open-access transmission line... connecting the electric grids in Utah and Nevada and expand access to next-generation geothermal developments in central Utah', 'set to support growing data center expansion in Utah and Nevada'; FAST-41 coverage granted 9 December 2025 and BLM EIS scoping (up to two lines, up to 600 kV, Millard County to Clark County) opened 2 September 2026 with comments to 5 October 2026. Bolo — 24 miles, 345 kV double-circuit, 800 MW bidirectional, New Mexico (above).
highlights: Southern Spirit is the one Pattern line with a regulatory fight: a 3:2 Louisiana vote after reconsideration, a state expropriation law written around it, an incumbent utility in opposition, more than half the Louisiana–Mississippi right-of-way unsecured as of January 2025 (Houston Chronicle) and a schedule that has slipped from 2029 to 2032

ERCOT's jurisdictional status is settled: FERC's May 2014 approval preserves ERCOT's independence and ERCOT and the PUCT confirmed in October 2024 that the DC tie does not bring Texas under FERC jurisdiction — the same problem Grid United's Pecos West could not get past a Texas certificate

Silver Rock is the first Pattern line framed around data-centre load and the first under the current administration's FAST-41 and Executive Order 14156 permitting track — the federal posture that has stalled onshore wind is being used to speed a wire

Derek Price's biography describes 'around 1,050 miles of new high-voltage transmission line that is planned to commence construction for Pattern over the next 2-3 years' — text that predates SunZia's completion and is the origin of the '1,100 miles' claim
productsAndServices.positioning: The only US developer with a delivered merchant HVDC line and a second one certificated in one of two states; Grid United (five lines, none certificated beyond Oklahoma) and Invenergy (Grain Belt, construction from 2026) are the peers. Where SunZia rode a subscriber model into CAISO, Southern Spirit relies on FERC negotiated-rate authority (modified in November 2016 to allocate 100% of capacity by open solicitation) and a DOE anchor contract that the current administration has not confirmed.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Merchant capacity under FERC negotiated-rate authority and open solicitations (Southern Spirit, Bolo, Silver Rock); build-own-transfer to a utility (Western Spirit to PNM); DOE Transmission Facilitation Program anchor contracts
targetSegments: Southeastern utilities and ERCOT generators (Southern Spirit)
Utah geothermal developers and Nevada/Utah data-centre load (Silver Rock)
New Mexico wind and the PNM system (Bolo)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Mississippi PSC decision on Southern Spirit (target was end-2025; still continued); MISO approval targeted 2028; construction 2029, in service 2032; Silver Rock EIS scoping to 5 October 2026; Bolo open solicitation (postponed)

productsAndServices.name: Solect Energy and Dynamic Energy — distributed commercial solar and storage affiliates
productsAndServices.category: Distributed generation (commercial solar, storage, EV charging)
productsAndServices.description: Solect Energy, 'a Pattern Energy company based in Hopkinton, Massachusetts, is a recognized leader in commercial solar... for commercial, light industrial, and institutional properties throughout the New England market'; at end-2024 it had 109 employees, 876 commercial projects completed, 177 MWdc installed, 15 MWh of storage, 540 customers and, per Solar Power World, the number-one commercial and industrial developer rank in Massachusetts by kilowatts installed in 2024, expanding into New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania; its site now counts 180 MW-plus, 900-plus projects and 730-plus service customers with 99% O&M renewal. Offerings: rooftop and ground-mount solar, canopies, storage, O&M, EV charging, PPA and site-lease financing. Dynamic Energy (Philadelphia, acquired 2022) has 'nearly 300 commercial and community solar, battery storage, and EV charging projects, totaling 688 MW of installed capacity in 15 states' and provided EPC for 16 projects totalling more than 45 MW in 2024; the 2026 About page names only Solect ('750+ commercial solar projects completed through our affiliate Solect Energy').
highlights: Acquired in 2021–22 as the take-private's diversification into distributed generation; the two affiliates are about 23% of group headcount (186 of 856) and a fraction of a percent of capacity

Solect's news feed is where Pattern's only tax-credit commentary appears — 'Town moves to quickly install Driscoll School solar project as Trump slashes clean energy tax credits' — the parent company has published nothing on the 2025 tax law
productsAndServices.positioning: A regional C&I developer with a top-10 national ranking (Solar Power World 2025), competing with Nexamp, Ameresco and local EPCs rather than with anything else in this corpus.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales to commercial, institutional and public-sector customers; PPA and site-lease financing; O&M contracts
targetSegments: New England and Mid-Atlantic commercial, industrial and institutional property owners
productsAndServices.roadmap: Geographic expansion into New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania (from 2024); no capacity target published

Neither was originated by Pattern; they are its only hyperscaler contracts on the record.

relationships.context: Pattern's project page describes the facility as 'helping Amazon Web Services achieve the goal of powering its operations with 100% renewable energy by 2025'. It is one of the earliest hyperscaler wind PPAs in the corpus and still in the fleet.

relationships.context: Pattern's October 2021 release on Phoenix Solar's start of operations names 'a 65 MWac, 12-year power purchase agreement with Digital Realty'; First Solar Series 6 modules, Nextracker trackers and Mortenson as builder.

relationships.note: The other private developer of interregional HVDC in the corpus — five pre-construction lines, family-office funded — against Pattern's operating SunZia and certificated Southern Spirit; Grid United's Southline and Pattern's SunZia and RioSol interest share the southern New Mexico–Arizona corridor, and Michael Skelly's Clean Line sold Western Spirit to Pattern.
relationships.context: MIT Technology Review's account of Clean Line's wind-down records the sale of Western Spirit 'to Pattern Development' as one of the three asset sales before Skelly's prior company shut in 2019 — Pattern finished that line in 2021. Today both companies court the same HVDC converter capacity at Hitachi Energy and the same DOE Transmission Facilitation Program, and both have a Texas-seam line (Southern Spirit with FERC's 2014 order; Pecos West denied by the PUCT in 2023). No commercial relationship between the two is on the record.

relationships.note: The other integrated renewables-and-transmission developer: Invenergy's Grain Belt Express (5,000 MW HVDC, construction from 2026) is the merchant comparable to SunZia and Southern Spirit, and both firms compete for the same DOE transmission programmes and Midwest wind sites.
relationships.context: DOE's October 2024 Transmission Facilitation Program round selected Pattern's Southern Spirit (up to USD 360 million) and Invenergy's Cimarron Link (up to USD 306 million) in the same USD 1.5 billion package; Invenergy then lost Grain Belt's USD 4.9 billion DOE loan guarantee in July 2025 and is proceeding privately. Invenergy is founder-controlled with Blackstone and CDPQ as investors; Pattern is pension-controlled — the two ownership models for the same asset class.

relationships.note: Entergy Mississippi's Wolf Creek substation in Choctaw County is Southern Spirit's eastern terminus, and Entergy Mississippi testified against the line at the Mississippi PSC.
relationships.context: The Louisiana PSC order describes Southern Spirit as running 'to Entergy Mississippi LLC's Wolf Creek Substation in Choctaw, Mississippi'. In October 2023 testimony Entergy Mississippi argued the line would 'very likely harm' its customers and that its Choctaw and Attala gas plants 'could not operate during periods with east-bound flow' — the incumbent utility as both interconnection host and opponent, which is why the Mississippi docket has been continued since 2017.

relationships.note: NextEra Energy Canadian Operating Services runs day-to-day operations at the ex-Cordelio Summerhaven wind and Moore solar facilities in Ontario that Pattern acquired in April 2026.
relationships.context: Pattern Canada's project pages for Summerhaven (124 MW) say 'day-to-day operations run by NextEra Energy Canadian Operating Services' and describe Moore Solar as a 'joint venture operated by NextEra Energy Canadian Operating Services'. An operating-services relationship inherited with Cordelio, recorded because the NextEra dossier is the place a reader would look for NextEra's Canadian O&M business.

policyExposure.regime: ITC/45X — OBBBA §45Y/§48E phase-down and the begin-construction test
policyExposure.exposure: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, wind and solar credits end for projects placed in service after 2027 unless they 'begin construction' by 4 July 2026; IRS Notice 2025-42 (August 2025) removed the 5% safe harbor for wind and large solar, and the D.C. district court vacated that notice on 6 June 2026, restoring it subject to appeal. Pattern's exposure is its US pipeline — Heritage Prairie Wind (construction from June 2026), Palomas, Lenawee, Uplands, The Shoals, Perryville, Big Island and the Michigan and Missouri wind projects it took from Cordelio. SunZia's credits are monetised through a USD 2.25 billion tax-equity term loan closed in 2023 and Nuveen's 'preferred tax equity for SunZia North'; the Nuveen release's risk language covers 'reduction, recapture, or disallowance of anticipated tax benefits'. Collection gap: no Pattern statement on OBBBA, the phase-down or FEOC exists on any company channel; the only tax-credit text is on the Solect affiliate's news feed.

policyExposure.regime: Federal wind permitting posture (Interior secretarial orders, BLM, Pentagon/FAA reviews) and FAST-41
policyExposure.exposure: Interior's July–August 2025 orders subjected wind projects to secretarial review and a 'capacity density' test, BLM removed onshore wind projects from its pipeline in March 2026, and Pentagon and FAA reviews are reported to be holding about 250 onshore projects on private land; Third Way's tracker cites SunZia as the exception that got built. Pattern's federal-land exposure going forward is Silver State Solar (BLM land) and any New Mexico or Nevada wind and solar on public land. The same administration granted Silver Rock Transmission FAST-41 coverage in December 2025 and opened its BLM scoping in September 2026 under Executive Order 14156.
policyExposure.mitigation: Pattern's stated advocacy posture — the chief executive on the American Clean Power Association board, positions at Advanced Energy United and ACORE, a political action committee — and a pipeline weighted to private land in Illinois, Michigan, Missouri, Arkansas, Louisiana and Canada.

policyExposure.regime: NHPA/NEPA litigation — Tohono O'odham Nation et al. v. U.S. Department of the Interior (SunZia)
policyExposure.exposure: The Ninth Circuit's 27 May 2025 opinion reversed the dismissal of the tribes' National Historic Preservation Act claim, holding that the BLM's two limited notices to proceed were final agency actions and that the plaintiffs plausibly alleged a failure to consult on a historic property treatment plan; on remand the plaintiffs' 13 March 2026 summary-judgment motion asks the court to nullify the BLM's construction authorisations in the San Pedro Valley. No injunction has ever issued; the line is operating. Archaeology Southwest also alleges the BLM granted the parallel RioSol line a right-of-way segment in May 2025 without tribal consultation.
policyExposure.mitigation: SunZia's position, per its spokesperson: construction in the San Pedro Valley is 'already complete' and the project remains on track; the company has not published a position on remedy.

policyExposure.regime: State siting and expropriation law — Louisiana SB 108 and Mississippi PSC (Southern Spirit)
policyExposure.exposure: Louisiana's SB 108 (August 2024) restricts expropriation for transmission lines not in an RTO plan or needed for reliability and was, per Louisiana Illuminator, crafted to target Southern Spirit; the LPSC's certificate (Order U-36669, 14 August 2024) passed 3:2 on reconsideration with a landowner challenge pending and a condition that no cost falls on Louisiana ratepayers. Mississippi's docket 2017-UA-79 remained 'CONTINUED' on the PSC's March and June 2026 agendas, past the company's end-2025 target, with Entergy Mississippi in opposition. As of January 2025 Pattern had not secured rights to more than half the Louisiana–Mississippi route and had paid landowners more than USD 6 million.
policyExposure.mitigation: Voluntary right-of-way acquisition; a Monroe, Louisiana office opened December 2023; the company's schedule now defers construction to 2029.

policyExposure.regime: FERC negotiated-rate authority and the CAISO Subscriber PTO model (merchant transmission)
policyExposure.exposure: SunZia's transmission is scheduled into California under the Subscriber Participating Transmission Owner model — 'the first entity to utilize the new SPTO policy' — with its capacity held by subscribers rather than allocated to all CAISO ratepayers (application January 2024, 3,021 MW; FERC Docket ER23-2917); SunZia Transmission LLC posts FERC Standards of Conduct because Pattern's marketing affiliates and the line's third-party operators must be separated, and on 1 April 2026 the line 'became affiliated with entities that employ marketing function employees' through the FERC-approved Cordelio acquisition. Southern Spirit holds FERC's May 2014 approval preserving ERCOT's independence and modified negotiated-rate authority (November 2016) to allocate all capacity by open solicitation; ERCOT and the PUCT confirmed in October 2024 that the DC tie does not bring Texas under FERC jurisdiction. Neither line sits in an Order 1920 regional plan, so neither receives regional cost allocation.

policyExposure.regime: DOE Transmission Facilitation Program and Energy Dominance Financing
policyExposure.exposure: Southern Spirit was selected on 3 October 2024 for a Transmission Facilitation Program capacity contract of 'up to $360 million' — DOE as anchor customer for part of the line's capacity — and no source confirms execution under the current administration. Separately, DOE's Energy Dominance Financing office closed a USD 489.4 million loan to Amanecer Puerto Rico LLC in August 2026 for 220 MW of standalone storage, framed by DOE under 'Unleashing American Energy' with domestically sourced batteries.
policyExposure.mitigation: Pattern describes Southern Spirit as 'privately funded' and has not made the federal contract a condition of the project on its own channels.

policyExposure.regime: Section 232 tariffs — steel and aluminium at 50%, transformer cores, and the wind-turbine investigation
policyExposure.exposure: Steel and aluminium duties rose to 50% on 3 June 2025 and were extended to distribution-transformer cores and laminations in August 2025; Commerce opened a Section 232 investigation into 'imports of wind turbines and their parts and components' on 13 August 2025, with analysts expecting 25–50%, and no proclamation had issued by September 2026. Exposure is the 2026–29 wind pipeline (Heritage Prairie, Palomas, Lenawee, Uplands, Broughton); SunZia's turbines were delivered before the measures. The company has not commented.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Pattern's strategy is to own the wires as well as the plants — to originate transmission where it controls the generation that fills it — and that SunZia's completion converts that thesis from a claim into a track record. Basis: the company's own 'Pattern Transmission' framing ('30 percent of the HVDC transmission lines in the United States'), the acquisition of SunZia Transmission after being awarded its full 3,000 MW for its wind, the Western Spirit build-own-transfer precedent, and three further lines (Southern Spirit, Bolo, Silver Rock) in development.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that Pattern is now a CPP Investments platform in substance — consolidating the fund's other North American renewables holdings (Cordelio) into it for shares — and that no exit process is under way. Basis: CPP's 69.1% statement; the share-based Cordelio deal from a wholly CPP-owned seller; the APG/ART entry as buyers of Riverstone's stake only; the absence of any sale, secondary, recapitalisation or IPO report in trade or financial press through September 2026. Collection gap: the precise split among CPP, APG/ABP, ART and management is not public.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that SunZia is financed to completion and contracted enough to service its debt, but that its equity returns are not knowable from outside. Basis: USD 11 billion of non-recourse facilities, HASI's USD 1.2 billion covering 'over 2.6 GW' of contracted capacity, Nuveen's USD 1.5 billion across four layers, and disclosed offtake of at least 1,175 MW (CPA 575, SRP 600) plus Shell, UC and six CCAs; against this, no final cost, no per-offtaker volumes, a rating-agency downgrade of the operating company in March 2025 and an unreadable August 2026 notes item.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Southern Spirit will not start construction before 2029 and may not proceed at all in its current form. Basis: the company's own schedule slipped from 2029 in-service to 2029 construction start; no Mississippi certificate nine years after filing; an incumbent (Entergy Mississippi) opposing at the interconnection point; Louisiana's expropriation law; more than half the right-of-way unsecured as of January 2025; a DOE anchor contract no source confirms was executed. The ERCOT jurisdictional question, by contrast, is settled in the project's favour.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the federal policy environment cuts both ways for Pattern and that the company has chosen silence over advocacy. Basis: onshore wind permitting and the OBBBA begin-construction test bear on a 2026–29 pipeline of at least 3.5 GW of named wind, while the same administration fast-tracked Silver Rock, lent USD 489 million to the Puerto Rico batteries and describes Pattern as delivering gas generation for PREPA; the company has published no statement on the tax law, tariffs or FEOC on any channel.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the company's headline pipeline figure (40 GW in 2026, from 25 GW in December 2024) reflects the Cordelio addition and a broadened definition rather than 15 GW of new origination, and that the audited-feeling measure of the platform is CPP's '5.6 GW developed since 2020'. Basis: Cordelio's 'over 18,000 MW' US pipeline of which Pattern took 'the majority'; three different company figures (25, 30, 40 GW) within eighteen months with no technology or geography breakdown. Stated at low confidence because the company publishes no reconciliation.
